*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health
emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of May 4, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
  electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative
  Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00
  A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
  number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and
  agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public
  hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the
  Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.
  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments:
  Members of the public can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make
  comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join
  the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception.
  Calls from landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing
  the phone line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is
  delayed from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.

  ¡ May 25, 2021 – Access Code: 2489941# wait two seconds and press # again

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your
  cable provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and
listen to the meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the
   3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and
listen to the meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the
Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in
appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of
the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and
regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-
related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or
offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or
service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-
412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301
or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later
than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  May 4, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
May 4, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Finance Authority Member/Parking
  Authority Member/Joint Powers Authority Member
  Dotson.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint
Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on
the Agendas.

Beverly Kenworthy, California Apartment Association, commented on Agenda Item O-1,
ordinance to amend Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and
Chapter 2, Article 3.

Rickie Williams spoke in favor of Agenda Item O-1, ordinance to amend Inglewood
Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and Chapter 2, Article 3.

Nathan Miller, Charter of National Renters Association, commented on Agenda Item O-
1, ordinance to amend Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and
Chapter 2, Article 3.

Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 4, resolution offering a
reward to any individual(s) that provides information leading to the identification,
apprehension, and conviction of the person(s) responsible for the death of Crystal
Crawford; 5, authorization of a purchase order from Thomson Reuters; and O-1
ordinance to amend Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and
Chapter 2, Article 3.

  1
 May 4, 2021

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills, and O-1, ordinance to amend
  Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and Chapter 2, Article 3.

  Mr. Okorie commented on Agenda Item No. O-1, ordinance to amend Inglewood
  Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10, and Chapter 2, Article 3.

  City Clerk Aisha Thompson read an email from Amber Kippler regarding Agenda Item
  No. O-1, ordinance to amend Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8, Articles 9 and 10,
  and Chapter 2, Article 3.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April
  29, 2021, in the amount of $1,286,188.31 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/ Successor Agency Member/ Housing Authority Member
  Dotson.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on September 22, 2020,
  and September 29, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None;
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Paula Gist Hawkins for alleged emotional and financial injuries on February 9, 2021.
  B. Deny Application for Leave to Present a Late Claim pursuant to Government
  Code, Section 911.6:
  1) Emely Castaneda for property damage; tree roots on April 27, 2021.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby reject claim listed as A-1, and deny the application for leave to
  present a late claim for the claim listed as B1. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 178  RESOLUTION NO. 21-88 ADOPTED – REWARD FOR IDENTIFICATION,
  APPREHENSION, AND CONVICTION OF THE PERSON(S) RESPONSIBLE
  FOR THE DEATH OF CRYSTAL CRAWFORD. Staff report dated May 4, 2021,
  was presented recommending adoption of a resolution offering a reward to any
  individual(s) that provides information leading to the identification, apprehension, and
  conviction of the person(s) responsible for the death of Crystal Crawford.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-88 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING A REWARD UP TO

  2
 May 4, 2021

  25,000 FOR INFORMATION LEADING TO THE IDENTIFICATION,
  APPREHENSION AND CONVICTION OF THE PERSON(S)
  RESPONSIBLE FOR THE HOMICIDE OF CRYSTAL CRAWFORD

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 178  PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED – THOMAS REUTERS. Staff report dated
  May 4, 2021, was presented recommending authorization of a purchase order from
  Thomson Reuters for access to the CLEAR database.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize the purchase order in the amount of $44,187.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 131.8  ORDINANCE NO. 21-09 INTRODUCED AS AMENDED – AMENDING
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 8, ARTICLES 9 AND 10, AND
  CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 3; RESOLUTION NO. 21-89 ADOPTED – TO INCLUDE
  HOUSING PROTECTION FEES IN MASTER FEE SCHEDULE. Staff report
  dated May 4, 2021, was presented recommending introduction of an Ordinance to amend
  Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 8 (Businesses, Trades, and Professions), Articles 9
  (Just Cause Eviction Protections) and 10 (Residential Rent Regulations), and Chapter 2
  (Administration), Article 3 (Boards and Commissions).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Yakema Decatur, Housing Protection Deputy Director/ Deputy to the City Manager,
  presented an Amended Housing Protection Ordinance to include: 1) Owners of properties
  of 5 or more units whose rents are less than 80% of fair market value, to be able to
  petition the Deputy Director for a rent increase of 5% plus the Consumer Price Index; 2)
  Owners of properties of 4 or less units whose rents are less than 80% of fair market value,
  to be able to petition the Deputy Director for an additional 2% rent increase (not to
  exceed 10%); and 3) Increase the maximum monthly allowance to recoup half of costs of
  a substantial remodel/capital improvement from $50 to $100.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City
  Council does hereby also include an amendment to the Ordinance to include waiving
  registration fees for owners whose rents are less than 70% of Fair Market Value,
  contingent upon registration being completed by the annual due dates. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-09 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2, SECTION 2-152.88 (RENTAL HOUSING BOARD)
  OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE, AND CHAPTER 8, ARTICLE 9 (
  JUST CAUSE EVICTION PROTECTIONS) AND ARTICLE 10
  (RESIDENTIAL RENT REGULATIONS) TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL
  PROTECTIONS FOR TENANTS AND OWNERS REGARDING
  RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTIES WITHIN THE CITY

  3
 May 4, 2021

  was introduced as amended by Council Member Padilla. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-89 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  ADOPTING FEES AND CHARGES SPECIFIC TO THE HOUSING
  PROTECTION DEPARTMENT AND AUTHORIZING THE INCLUSION OF
  SAID FEES AND CHARGES IN THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, thanked her
  colleagues for recognizing Annual City Clerk’s Week. She also reported about Cinco de
  Mayo and wished all mothers a Happy Mother’s Day.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at 2:45 p.m.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on Brown Act Violations and requested 3 minutes to
  discuss each agenda item. She also spoke about the parking Ordinance and asked the
  Council to respond to her emails and phone calls.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at 2:47 p.m.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke on the Police Oversight Commission and recommended it
  be brought back as soon as possible. He also requested an election schedule from the
  Council.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at 2:48 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at 2:49 p.m.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding a charge that was filed against him by
  Inglewood Police Department.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned, at the hour of 2:58 p.m.

  Approved this 21st day of September, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
